thesis: Shaytan's core strategy is not compulsion but the beautification of falsehood inside earthly life, and that strategy stops short of Allah's purified servants and never becomes true authority (sultan) except over those who choose to follow him.
notes: No fix needed. Beautification thesis is carried verbatim by three editions: al-Tabari on 15:39 reads la-uzayyinanna as 'la-uhassinanna lahum ma'asiyaka, wa la-uhabbibannaha ilayhim fi al-ard'; Ibn Kathir 'I will make sin dear to them'; al-Muyassar 'la-uhassinanna li-dhurriyyati Adama ma'asiyaka fi al-ard'. The sultan limit is grounded too (al-Tabari: 'laysa laka 'alayhim hujjah'; al-Muyassar: 'la aj'alu laka sultanan 'ala qulubihim tudilluhum bihi'; Ibn Kathir: 'you will have no way to reach those for whom I have decreed guidance'). QADAR CHECK (per task note): clean. The file frames 'bima aghwaytani' as Iblis's blame-psychology, which is Ibn Kathir's own framing ('the rebellion and arrogance of Iblis'); it never asserts or denies that Allah misguided him. Its translation 'because You let me fall into error' is in fact SOFTER than all four editions (al-Tabari: bi-ighwa'ika; Ibn Kathir: 'because You misled me and misguided me'), so there is no over-commitment in either direction. MUKHLASIN CHECK (per task note): clean and correctly non-elitist. The file's 'those whom Allah has purified... not self-authored heroism' matches al-Tabari exactly ('illa man akhlastahu bi-tawfiqika fa-hadaytahu') and al-Muyassar ('alladhina hadaytahum fa-akhlastahum li-ta'atika wa-tahhartahum'); the file keeps the referent broad ('Allah's servants') rather than inventing a spiritual elite, consistent with al-Dahhak and al-Jalalayn who both gloss it simply as 'the believers'. Only countable claim in the file is the g-w-y recurrence across 15:39/15:42 — verified in the corpus (aghwayta + ughwiya at 15:39, ghawin at 15:42). Two optional enrichments for the human, NOT errors: (1) the line 'It does not say merely the sincere in a purely self-generated sense' is true of the Hafs reading printed, but al-Tabari records the variant qira'ah al-mukhlisin (active) meaning precisely 'those who made their obedience sincere' — a sentence of ikhtilaf could be added; (2) al-Tabari glosses sultan as hujjah (argument/proof), a shade the file's 'enforceable mastery' does not carry, though Ibn Kathir and al-Muyassar both support the file's power-over reading.

thesis: Ash-Shu'ara's seventh and last prophet-narrative shows that rejection runs on a borrowed script (the rare Form II slur musahharin thrown at both Salih and Shu'ayb), and that the punishment arrived through the very shade the people ran toward, closing under the surah's eightfold refrain.

flags.quote: That is the entire reply. Eight words in English, four in Arabic.
flags.issue: The two counts do not measure the same span, so neither reading of the sentence is correct. The file's own English rendering of the reply is 'My Lord knows best what you do' = 6 words; it only reaches 8 by including 'He said'. The Arabic quoted is 'qala rabbi a'lamu bima ta'malun' = 5 orthographic words; it only reaches 4 by excluding 'qala'. Consistent counting gives either 8 English / 5 Arabic, or 6 English / 4 Arabic.

flags.quote: Ibn Kathir takes it as "those bewitched, unhinged by sorcery,"
flags.issue: Presented as a quotation from Ibn Kathir, but the fetched Ibn Kathir text says only: '(You are only one of those bewitched!) meaning, you are one of those who are affected by witchcraft.' The 'unhinged' element is not his — it belongs to al-Muyassar, who reads the phrase as 'mina alladhina asabahum al-sihru isabatan shadidatan, fa-dhahaba bi-'uqulihim' (took away their minds). Either re-attribute the mind-loss clause to al-Muyassar or drop it from the Ibn Kathir quote.

notes: Thesis and every structural claim are solid — the two flags are one-line copy fixes, not content problems, and nothing here touches the argument. VERIFIED MECHANICALLY: musahhar (Form II passive participle, root s-h-r) occurs exactly twice Quran-wide, 26:153 and 26:185, and the two verses are letter-for-letter identical after normalization (185-153 = 32 ayahs, as stated). mashur (Form I) occurs exactly 4 times across exactly 3 surahs: 15:15, 17:47, 17:101, 25:8 — matching the file's list and its note that 15:15 is the deniers speaking of themselves. The refrain 'inna fi dhalika la-ayatan wa ma kana aktharuhum mu'minin' occurs exactly 8 times, all inside Surah 26, at 8, 67, 103, 121, 139, 158, 174, 190 — the file's verse list is exact. The three frame lines each occur exactly 5 times within the surah and all fall inside 106-180: 'ala tattaqun' (106, 124, 142, 161, 177), 'inni lakum rasulun amin' (107, 125, 143, 162, 178), and the no-wage line (109, 127, 145, 164, 180); the Musa and Ibrahim sections carry none, as claimed. Lemma zullah: singular only at 7:171 and 26:189 (7:171 is indeed the simile of the mountain lifted 'ka-annahu zullah'), plural exactly 4 more occurrences at 2:210, 31:32 and twice in 39:16 ('zulalun mina-n-nar' above and below) — the file's counts are exactly right. TAFSIR ATTRIBUTIONS VERIFIED: al-Tabari's jibillah gloss 'al-khalq al-awwalin' and his note that the Arabs had two forms of the word ('wa fi al-jibillah li-l-'arab lughatan'); al-Muyassar's 'al-umam al-mutaqaddima 'alaykum'; Ibn Zayd's recitation of 36:62 in this very passage; al-Tabari's second reading of musahhar ('mu'allal tu'allal bi-l-ta'ami wa-l-sharabi kama nu'allalu bihima, wa lasta malakan'); al-Muyassar's taunt ('fa-in kunta sadiqan... fa-'du Allaha an yusqita 'alayna qita'a 'adhabin mina-s-sama'') — all match the fetched text. The heat / cloud / rush-for-shade / it-became-fire narrative is carried by Ibn Kathir and by al-Tabari's Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah, Ibn Jurayj, ad-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd reports. ADAB: the Aykah-vs-Madyan question is explicitly acknowledged as a matter the tradition debates, which is exactly right — Qatadah in al-Tabari holds Shu'ayb was sent to two communities. No truncation artifacts; no ahkam exposure.

thesis: Al-Hijr closes by naming the Prophet's chest-constriction rather than denying it, and prescribes tasbih, sujud and unbroken worship until al-yaqin — death — as the way through, with sufficiency rather than resolution as the promised relief.
notes: No fix needed; this file is unusually well-sourced and handles the one dangerous reading correctly. AL-YAQIN CHECK (per task note): the file does exactly what the note requires. It names the deviant reading — 'Some have suggested that al-yaqin names a spiritual rank — that once a worshipper reaches certainty, the obligation of worship falls away' — and immediately closes it: 'The classical commentary leaves no opening for that reading.' That is the correct handling and it matches Ibn Kathir, who is far blunter in the fetched text: 'it is a mistake to interpret Yaqin as Ma'rifah as some of the Sufis do. According to them, when one of them attains the level of Ma'rifah, they consider him to be free of these obligations. This is disbelief, misguidance and ignorance.' The death-reading is unanimous across all four editions fetched (al-Jalalayn: 'al-mawt'; al-Muyassar: 'wa huwa al-mawt'; al-Tabari: 'hatta ya'tiyaka al-mawt'; Ibn Kathir via al-Bukhari and Salim). EVERY NAMED ATTRIBUTION VERIFIED VERBATIM: al-Tabari's second word of narrowness 'yuhrijuk' (root h-r-j) for the constriction; al-Muyassar's 'inqibad sadrika'; al-Tabari's two named contents of 'what they say' — 'takdhibihim iyyaka wa-stihza'ihim bika wa bima ji'tahum bihi' — including the file's observation of the double target (the Messenger himself and what he brought); al-Tabari's verb of alarm 'fa-fza'' plus the Prophet's habit ('kana idha hazabahu amrun fazi'a ila al-salah'); the sufficiency promise in both al-Tabari ('yakfika Allahu min dhalika ma ahammak') and al-Muyassar ('fa-inna dhalika yakfika ma ahammak'); al-Muyassar's gloss of al-sajidin as 'al-musallin lillahi al-'abidin lahu'; the chain to Salim ibn Abdullah answering in one word 'al-mawt', followed by 'wa bi-nahwi alladhi qulna fi dhalika qala ahlu al-ta'wil'; al-Tabari's grammatical parallel of the active form doing passive work, 'khamrun 'atiq wa hiya mu'attaqah' — the file's 'aged wine' example is his, exactly; and al-Muyassar's closing 'imtathala Rasulullahi sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam amra rabbihi, fa-lam yazal da'iban fi 'ibadati-llahi hatta atahu al-yaqinu min rabbih'. No countable or absolute claims in the file requiring corpus verification. No truncation artifacts; no ahkam exposure.
